classification.difficultyReason: Identify reflections or rotations from equations, including simplifying signs in shifted reciprocal expressions, then transfer intercepts, vertices and asymptotes to sketches. The reciprocal cases require the most coordination of algebra and graphical features.

content.prompt: For each equation, determine whether the subsequent equation is a reflection or a rotation of the first equation, then sketch each graph.

spec.description: Four axis-only coordinate scaffolds aligned with the four equations. No grid is printed.
spec.mathematics: Each panel has unit ticks, labels at −4, −2, 2 and 4 on both axes, and arrowed axes.
spec.answerVisibility: The supplied blue exponential curves are omitted from the student scaffolds.

answer.short: Relative to $f(x)=3^x$, in equation order after the reference: $-f(x)$, reflection across the $x$-axis; $-f(-x)$, rotation of $180^\circ$ about the origin; $f(-x)$, reflection across the $y$-axis.
answer.worked:
Let $f(x)=3^x$. Reflect using the coordinate rules $(x,y)\mapsto(x,-y)$, $(x,y)\mapsto(-x,-y)$ and $(x,y)\mapsto(-x,y)$ respectively.
$$\begin{aligned}-f(x)&=-3^x\quad\text{Reflection in the x-axis}\\-f(-x)&=-3^{-x}\quad\text{180-degree rotation about the origin}\\f(-x)&=3^{-x}\quad\text{Reflection in the y-axis}\end{aligned}$$
The four graphs pass through $(0,1)$, $(0,-1)$, $(0,-1)$ and $(0,1)$ respectively. All approach the horizontal asymptote $y=0$ without meeting it. The reference graph is increasing and positive; the other graphs are decreasing and negative, increasing and negative, and decreasing and positive respectively.

spec.description: Four completed exponential graphs in equation order; every image is an exact axis reflection or half-turn of the reference.
spec.mathematics: Graphs of 3^x, −3^x, −3^(−x), 3^(−x); horizontal asymptote y=0 is not drawn.

answer.short: Relative to $f(x)=(x-1)^2$, in equation order after the reference: $-f(x)$, reflection across the $x$-axis; $f(-x)$, reflection across the $y$-axis; $-f(-x)$, rotation of $180^\circ$ about the origin.
answer.worked:
Let $f(x)=(x-1)^2$.
$$\begin{aligned}-f(x)&=-(x-1)^2\quad\text{Reflection in the x-axis}\\f(-x)&=(-x-1)^2\quad\text{Reflection in the y-axis}\\&=(x+1)^2\\-f(-x)&=-(x+1)^2\quad\text{180-degree rotation about the origin}\end{aligned}$$
Reflect the reference vertex $(1,0)$ and its points in the required axes. The vertices, in equation order, are $(1,0)$, $(1,0)$, $(-1,0)$ and $(-1,0)$. The parabolas open upwards, downwards, upwards and downwards respectively. Their $y$-intercepts are $1,-1,1,-1$.

spec.description: Four completed parabolas with continuation arrows; no invented vertex labels.
spec.mathematics: Vertices (1,0), (1,0), (−1,0), (−1,0), with opening directions up, down, up, down.

answer.short: Relative to $f(x)=4-x$, in equation order after the reference: $-f(x)$, reflection across the $x$-axis; $f(-x)$, reflection across the $y$-axis; $-f(-x)$, rotation of $180^\circ$ about the origin.
answer.worked:
Let $f(x)=4-x$.
$$\begin{aligned}-f(x)&=-(4-x)\quad\text{Reflection in the x-axis}\\&=x-4\\f(-x)&=4-(-x)\quad\text{Reflection in the y-axis}\\&=x+4\\-f(-x)&=-(4+x)\quad\text{180-degree rotation about the origin}\\&=-x-4\end{aligned}$$
Reflect the reference intercepts $(0,4)$ and $(4,0)$. The four lines have intercept pairs $(0,4),(4,0)$; $(0,-4),(4,0)$; $(0,4),(-4,0)$; and $(0,-4),(-4,0)$ respectively. Draw each straight line through its pair of intercepts.

spec.description: Four completed straight-line graphs with continuation arrows.
spec.mathematics: Graphs of 4−x, x−4, x+4 and −x−4, with the source intercepts and slopes.

answer.short: Relative to $f(x)=1+\dfrac{1}{x-1}$, in equation order after the reference: $f(-x)$, reflection across the $y$-axis; $-f(-x)$, rotation of $180^\circ$ about the origin; $-f(x)$, reflection across the $x$-axis.
answer.worked:
Let $f(x)=1+\dfrac{1}{x-1}$.
$$\begin{aligned}f(-x)&=1+\frac{1}{-x-1}\quad\text{Reflection in the y-axis}\\&=1-\frac{1}{x+1}\\-f(-x)&=-1+\frac{1}{x+1}\quad\text{180-degree rotation about the origin}\\-f(x)&=-1-\frac{1}{x-1}\quad\text{Reflection in the x-axis}\\&=-1+\frac{1}{1-x}\end{aligned}$$
Reflect the reference curve and its asymptotes using the same coordinate rules. All four graphs pass through $(0,0)$. Their vertical asymptotes, in equation order, are $x=1,-1,-1,1$; their horizontal asymptotes are $y=1,1,-1,-1$. Draw two separate branches in each panel, approaching the asymptotes.

spec.description: Four completed rational graphs, obtained by reflecting the same reference branches. Dashed vertical asymptotes are retained; horizontal asymptote lines and labels are not added.
spec.mathematics: All graphs cross the origin. Vertical asymptotes x=1,−1,−1,1 and horizontal limits y=1,1,−1,−1 respectively.
